transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 15:00 PT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Tom (Cerulean Head of ML), Priya (Platform Eng), David (CTO)

Summary: quick discovery focused on latency and throughput needs for Cerulean's payment fraud and reconciliation features. Discussed p95 latency targets, concurrency, streaming preferences, and benchmarking plan. Action items and next steps captured.

00:00 Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro from our side, i'm maya, i'm the account lead, jordan's our se and he'll cover benchmarks.
00:18 Tom (Cerulean): hey thanks, quick context: Cerulean processes merchant reconciliation and a realtime fraud signal pipeline. We need inference for short prompts (single-turn heuristic checks) and longer summarization for dispute docs.
00:35 Priya: our rough qps is 120 reqs/s at peak, peak bursts to 250 for a few minutes. most requests are short (like 8-30 tokens output) but we also have batch jobs that stream longer outputs. p95 latency is our big SLO.
00:50 Jordan (Redwood): good, can you share p95 targets? are you trying to hit p95 < 200ms for the short ones? or lower?
01:02 Tom: ideally p95 < 150ms for the short checks; for longer streaming summarizations p95 under 1s for first token and throughput matters for tokens/sec.
01:20 David (CTO): and security: we need VPC, KMS, audit logs, and SOC2 compliance. if we go private/on-prem that's an option but incurs ops.
01:34 Maya: got it. we typically advise: Hosted for very fast onboarding, Dedicated for predictable throughput (reserved GPU pools) and Private for regulated or air-gapped. we'll map those to your p95 and concurrency needs.
01:50 Jordan: quick numbers — on a typical F32/8 GPU profile (demo language model), we can achieve ~3k-6k tokens/sec aggregate depending on quantization and batch settings; for short 8–30-token responses that often translates into p95s in the 80–200ms range on dedicated capacity with proper batching and prefix caching. on hosted the tail can be a bit higher depending on multi-tenant peaks.
02:18 Priya: what's the behavior for streaming? we need first-byte latency low and steady token/sec afterwards.
02:28 Jordan: streaming first-byte is influenced by scheduling/batching windows; we can configure low-latency streaming lanes with smaller batch windows (sacrificing some cost efficiency). we often set a fast-path for low-latency streaming with a p95 first-token SLA.
02:45 Tom: curious about concurrency: we'll have 200 concurrent short requests, sometimes spikes to 400 for flash events. how does Redwood handle that?
02:58 Jordan: autoscaling + reserved capacity on Dedicated: you can reserve n GPUs to cover baseline QPS and configure burst capacity. routing policies can route latency-sensitive traffic to premium lanes. for Hosted we rely on dynamic autoscale but you'd see more variance in tail latency at big spikes.
03:18 Priya: any guidance on tokens/sec per GPU so we can size reserved capacity?
03:25 Jordan: a rough thumb: a single high-end A100/80GB equiv can do ~4k-12k tokens/sec depending on model size and quantization. smaller models or int8 quantization pushes higher tokens/sec. we provide model profiles in the catalog. we'll run a baseline with your prompts to get concrete numbers.
03:48 Maya: we've seen customers trade a few ms of average latency for 20–30% cost reductions by enabling prefix/KV cache and delta quantization. might be relevant for your batch dispute jobs.
04:02 David: on private deployment—what's the deployment time and ops cost? our security team is strict.
04:12 Jordan: Private (VPC or on-prem) usually takes longer: there's a private control plane setup, KMS/HSM integration, and network peering. timeline ranges 6–12 weeks depending on infra. Dedicated is faster—usually a few weeks to reserve and tune capacity. Hosted is immediate.
04:34 Tom: for benchmarks — we want p95 numbers for our real prompts, not synthetic. can you run token/sec and p95 across three scenarios: hosted baseline, dedicated reserved config, private (if possible) or equivalent isolated instance?
04:50 Jordan: yep, we can. we'll need sample prompts, expected concurrency pattern, and whether streaming is used. we'll run streaming and non-streaming runs and return CSV with p50/p90/p95/p99 and tokens/sec. link to example benchmark spreadsheet: https://redwood-internal.example.com/benchmarks/cerulean-template (placeholder)
05:12 Priya: about costs — can you share typical per-token breakdown and how batching impacts price?
05:20 Maya: yes i'll include a cost examples doc. generally, batching improves cost per token but increases scheduling latency. for short, latency-sensitive calls we recommend smaller batch windows or dedicated lanes. for long outputs, larger batches and caching really cut cost.
05:38 Tom: any gotchas with KV cache and concurrency? our queries sometimes reuse prefixes for a merchant.
05:45 Jordan: KV cache helps a lot for repeated prefixes — reduces compute per token. the tradeoff is additional memory per instance; Dedicated lets you choose profiles with larger KV capacities. we'll profile your prefix reuse.
06:03 Priya: compliance questions: does hosted store logs long-term? we need audit logs and retention controls.
06:11 Maya: yes we provide audit logs and retention options as an add-on; Private gives you full control of log retention; Dedicated isolates customer data but control plane logs are still managed by Redwood with configurable retention. we'll attach SOC2/ISO artifacts.
06:30 David: who will run the benchmark and how will we validate results?
06:36 Jordan: we'll run the Redwood benchmark harness with your prompts; results include raw latencies, payload sizes, and token/sec; we can run side-by-side with an internal baseline model or a customer-supplied baseline if you prefer. export as CSV and share link.
06:58 Tom: ok good. timeline?
07:02 Maya: we'll target sending pricing & security docs by Friday (2026-03-06). Jordan will run the benchmark and aim for 2026-03-09 results. Cerulean to send sample prompts and traffic patterns by 2026-03-05.
07:18 Priya: also can we get recommended Dedicated config (GPU type, reserved count) for our 250 peak qps scenario?
07:25 Jordan: yes we'll produce a sizing recommendation after the benchmark — include latency targets (p95 150ms short, first-token streaming < 200ms).
07:40 Tom: competitors we tried — OpenAI was ok but tail latency was an issue at scale; Anthropic had good quality but cost was higher. we'll be evaluating head-to-head on latency/cost.
07:58 Maya: noted. we'll include a comparative note.
08:05 David: contract/legal — any standard terms for Dedicated reserved capacity?
08:10 Maya: standard monthly commit with exit/overage terms; i'll share the draft.
08:18 Priya: small transcription note: could you also include notes on how to set up SSO for our tenant?
08:24 Maya: yes, SSO/SAML docs included in security pack.
08:30 Closing recap: p95 target short queries 150ms, streaming first-token < 200ms, concurrency peaks 250 with bursts to 400; Redwood to run benchmarks (Jordan) and share pricing/security pack (Maya).
08:52 Tom: thanks everyone. that was helpful.
09:00 End meeting

Notes: transcript includes occasional mis-heard words; Redwood product names referred to casually (e.g., "Redwood dedicated", "Redwood private", "redwood runtime") and sometimes mis-capitalized in chat. Links referenced as placeholders for docs and benchmark spreadsheets.
